questions.stem: How does the Point-to-Point (PP) integration model connect applications?
options: Every application connects with every other application directly
Every application connects only to one central hub
Applications connect through a message queue only
Applications never connect; data is moved manually
Only two applications may exist in the model
questions.explanation: The Point-to-Point model connects all applications with each other, so with five applications there will be many connections.

questions.stem: In the Hub-and-Spoke model, how do applications connect?
options: Each application connects with every other application
All applications connect only with one centralised hub
Applications connect in a ring, each to its neighbour
Applications connect to several regional hubs at once
Applications share a single database table
questions.explanation: The Hub-and-Spoke model creates a new centralised connection point called the Hub, and all applications connect ONLY with that one Hub.

questions.stem: Which of the following are given as examples of the Hub-and-Spoke model?
options: Spreadsheets, email and file shares
Web servers, load balancers and caches
Dimensional Data Warehouse, Data Hub and Data Fabric
Mobile apps and browser extensions
Firewalls and VPNs
questions.explanation: Examples of the Hub-and-Spoke model are the dimensional Data Warehouse, Data Hub and Data Fabric, which serve as a single point of truth for all enterprise users.

questions.stem: Why is security considered better in the Hub-and-Spoke model than in Point-to-Point?
options: Because the hub encrypts every message automatically
Because Point-to-Point has no authentication at all
Because the hub is hosted off-site
Because all users connect to one centralised hub, so the risk of a security breach is lower
Because Hub-and-Spoke uses fewer applications
questions.explanation: As all users connect to one centralised Hub, the risk of a security breach is less in the Hub-and-Spoke model than in Point-to-Point.

questions.stem: How does the Hub-and-Spoke model handle user access compared with Point-to-Point?
options: It removes the need for user access management
It requires each application to manage its own access matrix
It grants all users the same permissions
It delegates access to the source systems
It manages the user access matrix at a centralised place
questions.explanation: The Hub-and-Spoke model can manage the user access matrix at a centralised place, unlike the Point-to-Point model.

questions.stem: Why is the Hub-and-Spoke model described as more flexible than Point-to-Point?
options: The hub makes it easy to incorporate new requirements without implementing them in source systems
Each application can be replaced without any change to the hub
It has no fixed data model
It works without any initial investment
It supports only one application at a time
questions.explanation: In the Hub-and-Spoke model, the Hub makes it easy to incorporate new requirements that do not need to be implemented in source systems.

questions.stem: What is said about the cost of the Hub-and-Spoke model?
options: It is always cheaper from day one with no initial investment
It requires initial investment, but afterwards new requirements are much cheaper because changes go into the hub
It is more expensive than Point-to-Point in every case
Cost is identical to Point-to-Point
Cost depends only on the number of users
questions.explanation: Hub implementation requires initial investment, but once implemented, new requirements have a much cheaper impact because all changes go into the Hub rather than into each application.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an advantage of Hub-and-Spoke over Point-to-Point?
options: Better user access management
Lower security breach risk
Greater flexibility for new requirements
Zero implementation effort
Cheaper handling of new requirements after initial investment
questions.explanation: Hub-and-Spoke is better in access management, security, flexibility and cost, but it does require an initial investment to implement the Hub.

questions.stem: In the Point-to-Point model, where must a new requirement be implemented?
options: Only in the central hub
Only in the data warehouse
In each application
In the semantic layer
Nowhere; requirements are handled automatically
questions.explanation: In the Point-to-Point model changes must be made in each application, whereas in Hub-and-Spoke all changes go into the Hub.

questions.stem: Hub-and-Spoke examples such as the Data Warehouse, Data Hub and Data Fabric serve what role for enterprise users?
options: A backup archive
A development sandbox
A message broker
A firewall
A single point of truth
questions.explanation: The dimensional Data Warehouse, Data Hub and Data Fabric serve as a single point of truth for all enterprise users.
